Section: ## Stage 1
Part 2 of 2

## Stage 1

## Completion of the Claim Notification Form

## 6.1

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.1] (1) The claimant must complete and send—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.1] (a) the CNF to the defendant’s insurer, if known; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.1] (b) the Defendant Only Claim Notification Form (“Defendant Only CNF”) to the defendant,

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.1] but the requirement to send the form to the defendant may be ignored in a disease claim where the CNF has been sent to the insurer and the defendant has been dissolved, is insolvent or has ceased to trade.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.1] (2) If—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.1] (a) the insurer’s identity is not known; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.1] (b) the defendant is known not to hold insurance cover, the CNF must be sent to the defendant’s registered office or principal place of business and no Defendant Only CNF is required.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.1] (3) Where the insurer’s identity is not known, the claimant must make a reasonable attempt to identify the insurer and, in an employers’ liability claim, the claimant must have carried out a database search through the Employers’ Liability Tracing Office.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.1] (4) In a disease claim, the CNF should be sent to the insurer identified as the insurer last on risk for the employer for the material period of employment.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.1] 6.2 If the CNF or Defendant Only CNF cannot be sent to the defendant via the prescribed Portal address, it must be sent via first class post; and this must be done, in a case where the CNF is sent to the insurer, at the same time or as soon as practicable after the CNF is sent.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.1] 6.3 All boxes in the CNF that are marked as mandatory must be completed before it is sent.  The claimant must make a reasonable attempt to complete those boxes that are not marked as mandatory.

## 6.4 Where the claimant is a child, this must be noted in the relevant section of the CNF.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.4 Where the claimant is a child, this must be noted in the relevant section of the CNF.] 6.5 The statement of truth in the CNF must be signed either by the claimant or by the claimant’s legal representative where the claimant has authorised the legal representative to do so and the legal representative can produce written evidence of that authorisation. Where the claimant is a child the statement of truth may be signed by the parent or guardian.  On the electronically completed CNF the person may enter their name in the signature box to satisfy this requirement.

## Rehabilitation

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > Rehabilitation] 6.6 The claimant must set out details of rehabilitation in the CNF. The parties should at all stages consider the Rehabilitation Code which may be found at: http://www.iua.co.uk/IUA_Member/Publications (opens in a new tab)

## Failure to complete the Claim Notification Form

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > Failure to complete the Claim Notification Form] 6.7 Where the defendant considers that inadequate mandatory information has been provided in the CNF that shall be a valid reason for the defendant to decide that the claim should no longer continue under this Protocol.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > Failure to complete the Claim Notification Form] 6.8 Rule 45.35(2) sets out the sanctions available to the court where it considers that the claimant provided inadequate information in the CNF.

## Response

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > Response] 6.9 The defendant must send to the claimant an electronic acknowledgment the next day after receipt of the CNF.

## 6.10 If the claimant has sent the CNF to the defendant in accordance with paragraph 6.1(2)—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.10 If the claimant has sent the CNF to the defendant in accordance with paragraph 6.1(2)—] (a) the defendant must send to the claimant an electronic acknowledgment the next day after receipt of the CNF and send the CNF to the insurer at the same time and advise the claimant that they have done so;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.10 If the claimant has sent the CNF to the defendant in accordance with paragraph 6.1(2)—] (b) the insurer must send to the claimant an electronic acknowledgment  the next day after its receipt by the insurer;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.10 If the claimant has sent the CNF to the defendant in accordance with paragraph 6.1(2)—] and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.10 If the claimant has sent the CNF to the defendant in accordance with paragraph 6.1(2)—] (c) the claimant must then submit the CNF to the insurer via the Portal as soon as possible and, in any event, within 30 days of the day upon which the claimant first sent it to the defendant.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.10 If the claimant has sent the CNF to the defendant in accordance with paragraph 6.1(2)—] 6.11 The defendant must complete the ‘Response’ section of the CNF (“the CNF response”) and send it to the claimant—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.10 If the claimant has sent the CNF to the defendant in accordance with paragraph 6.1(2)—] (a) in the case of an employers’ liability claim, within 30 days of the step taken pursuant to paragraph 6.1; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > 6.10 If the claimant has sent the CNF to the defendant in accordance with paragraph 6.1(2)—] (b) in the case of a public liability claim, within 40 days of the step taken pursuant to paragraph 6.1.

## Application for a certificate of recoverable benefits

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > Application for a certificate of recoverable benefits] 6.12 The defendant must, before the end of Stage 1, apply to the Compensation Recovery Unit (CRU) for a certificate of recoverable benefits.

## Contributory Negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > Contributory Negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] 6.13 The claim will no longer continue under this Protocol where the defendant, within the relevant period in paragraph 6.11 —

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > Contributory Negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (1) makes an admission of liability but alleges contributory negligence;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > Contributory Negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (2) does not complete and send the CNF response;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > Contributory Negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (3) does not admit liability; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > Contributory Negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (4) notifies the claimant that the defendant considers that—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > Contributory Negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (a) there is inadequate mandatory information in the CNF; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > Contributory Negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (b) if proceedings were issued, the small claims track would be the normal track for that claim.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > Contributory Negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] 6.14 Where the defendant does not admit liability the defendant must give brief reasons in the CNF response.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > Contributory Negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] 6.15 Where paragraph 6.13 applies the claim will proceed under the relevant Pre-Action Protocol and the CNF will serve as the letter of claim (except where the claim no longer continues under this Protocol because the CNF contained inadequate information).  Time will be treated as running under the relevant Pre-Action Protocol from the date the form of acknowledgment is served under paragraph 6.9 or 6.10.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > Contributory Negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (For admissions made in the course of the process under this Protocol, see rule 14.1B.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > Contributory Negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (Paragraph 2.10A of the Pre-Action Protocol on Personal Injury and paragraph 6.10A of the Pre-Action Protocol for Disease and Illness Claims provide that the CNF can be used as the letter of claim except where the claim no longer continues under this Protocol because the CNF contained inadequate information.)

## Stage 1 fixed costs

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > Stage 1 fixed costs] 6.16 Except where the claimant is a child, where liability is admitted the defendant must pay the Stage 1 fixed costs in Table 11 in Practice Direction 45 within 10 days after receiving the Stage 2 Settlement Pack.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims > Stage 1 fixed costs] 6.17 Where the defendant fails to pay the Stage 1 fixed costs within the period specified in paragraph 6.16 the claimant may give written notice that the claim will no longer continue under this Protocol.  Unless the claimant’s notice is sent to the defendant within 10 days after the expiry of the period in paragraph 6.16 the claim will continue under this Protocol.
